runs.goal_hypothesis: Reproduce the original strong heuristic results under the recorded 5.12M-step PPO configuration.

results_insights.insight: The reproduction reached a 49.17% terminal average win rate.
The aggregate concealed a 1% worst-matchup floor.
A 94% offensive-X win rate confirms strong but asymmetric competence.

reasoning: The PPO configuration reproduced high average heuristic performance.
The 1% worst rate shows reproduction of the aggregate did not imply robust policy/side coverage.
This is a configuration reproduction rather than a random-seed replication, so sampling and uncontrolled historical differences remain.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Continue the reproduced model from one loaded snapshot to test whether additional self-play preserves its heuristic performance.

results_insights.insight: Continuation ended 12.67 percentage points below the 49.17% reproduction.
The robustness floor fell to zero.
Offensive-X dropped sharply from 94% in the reproduced predecessor.

reasoning: Additional snapshot-based training caused catastrophic forgetting in offensive-X competence.
Removing random warmup and using a 3.072M continuation changed the experienced opponent distribution.
Because this is a continuation with several schedule changes, the loss cannot be attributed solely to elapsed training.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Train a longer fresh schedule to determine whether catastrophic forgetting is reproducible without a loaded continuation snapshot.

results_insights.insight: The fresh long run retained 47.17% average performance, near the 49.17% reproduction.
At least one matchup still had zero wins.
Offensive-X remained at 93%, unlike the loaded continuation's 17%.

reasoning: Forgetting was not inevitable with more fresh-schedule training; offensive-X remained strong.
The loaded continuation's altered starting distribution is a more likely cause of its collapse than duration alone.
Multiple schedule horizons differ from the 5.12M reproduction, and the zero worst rate still shows unresolved asymmetry.
